evidence: bare_number_card: seg1:mid and seg1:end are just the text '$1,000B' and '2025' floating above a hairline timeline — no filling, stacking or comparison; the number is stated, not demonstrated.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: At seg1:mid the whole composition is a single horizontal timeline sitting at ~45% height with tick labels 2007–2025, the words '$1,000B' and '2025' in low-contrast grey overlapping the ticks, and Data shrunk to ~8% of frame height straddling the line; everything below y≈350 is empty gradient. seg1:end repeats the identical layout with the marker parked at the right end — two near-identical beats spending 8s of a 50s video on one unillustrated number.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The scene plan hands this beat a 'timeline scrub' visual that is intrinsically a 1-D line in a 16:9 mental model, so it renders as a thin band in a vertical frame with no secondary element authored to occupy the lower two-thirds, and the value is drawn as a floating label instead of a quantity with physical extent.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Replace the bare timeline with a vertical-native demonstration of the 2007→2025 climb that fills the frame: stack or grow the value downward through the empty region (e.g. a column that fills bottom-to-top past 2007's $589B mark to $1T, or accumulating unit blocks), keep the year label attached to the growing element rather than free-floating, raise label contrast off the dark gradient, and give Data an action tied to the growth (pushing/riding the fill upward and reacting when it crosses $1T) rather than perching on a line.
